beijing.fact: The name means "northern capital"; it has been China's capital for most of the last 800 years.

tianjin.fact: Beijing's port city, half an hour away by high-speed train.

hebei.fact: "North of the river" (the Yellow River); it wraps all the way around Beijing and Tianjin.

shanxi.fact: "West of the mountains"; China's coal heartland. Not to be confused with Shaanxi next door.

inner-mongolia.fact: Stretches about 2,400 km along the Mongolian border, touching eight other provinces.

liaoning.fact: Shenyang was the Qing dynasty's capital before it moved to Beijing.

jilin.fact: Borders North Korea and Russia; Changchun is a major car-making city.

heilongjiang.fact: Named for the "Black Dragon River" (the Amur); Harbin's ice festival is world famous.

shanghai.fact: China's largest city and financial center, at the mouth of the Yangtze.

jiangsu.fact: One of China's richest provinces; Suzhou's classical gardens are here.

zhejiang.fact: Home of Alibaba and West Lake, and the heart of China's private-business economy.

anhui.fact: Home to the Yellow Mountains (Huangshan), a classic subject of Chinese painting.

fujian.fact: Faces Taiwan across the strait; the word "tea" came to English from its local dialect.

jiangxi.fact: Jingdezhen here has made porcelain for over a thousand years.

shandong.fact: Birthplace of Confucius; Qingdao, and its beer, are here.

henan.fact: The cradle of Chinese civilization, home of the Shaolin Temple.

hubei.fact: The Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest power station, is here.

hunan.fact: Mao Zedong's home province, known for fiery food and the Zhangjiajie pillar mountains.

guangdong.fact: China's most populous province and biggest economy; home of Cantonese and Shenzhen.

guangxi.fact: Guilin's karst hills are here; the Zhuang are China's largest ethnic minority.

hainan.fact: A tropical island province, China's smallest province by land.

hong-kong.fact: A British colony until 1997; now runs under "one country, two systems."

macau.fact: Portuguese until 1999; one of the most densely populated places on Earth.

chongqing.fact: China's wartime capital in WWII; its municipality is roughly the size of Austria.

sichuan.fact: Home of giant pandas and numbing Sichuan pepper.

guizhou.fact: Mountainous and misty, and home to Moutai, China's most famous liquor.

yunnan.fact: "South of the clouds"; China's most ethnically diverse province, and the origin of Pu'er tea.

tibet.fact: Averages over 4,000 m above sea level; Everest sits on its border with Nepal.

shaanxi.fact: Home of the Terracotta Army; Xi'an was the eastern end of the Silk Road.

gansu.fact: A long, thin corridor that carried the Silk Road west; the Great Wall ends here.

qinghai.fact: Named for Qinghai Lake, China's largest; the Yangtze and Yellow rivers start here.

ningxia.fact: Homeland of the Hui Muslims, and a growing wine region.

xinjiang.fact: China's largest division, a sixth of the country; it borders eight countries.
